case of the flow through curved interfaces, and `write_openfoam` warns of a flow through a
conforming mesh.

Checked (`tests/test_code_aster.py`, `tests/test_openfoam.py`; `tests/fake_code_aster.py`
and `tests/fake_openfoam.py` stand in for the programs, with their own readers of the
files and their own linear elements or finite volumes): the meshes in Code_Aster's format
read back node for node, element for element and group for group, every line within 80

$1.8\cdot10^{-13}$ and $8\cdot10^{-14}$ (kinematic); cubic crystals and orthotropic

0.15, within $10^{-12}$; a random medium of 10 × 8 × 8 voxels at 69 % of pores, the

$3\cdot10^{-13}$ (0.3389 with symmetry planes, 0.3764 with cyclic faces: the closed pores,
0.6 % of the box, left out in the first); the flow rate read back to the permeability.

**Code_Aster itself** (18.1.11 of conda-forge, `run_code_aster`;

## 112. The credibility of the simulations with VIMSEO (`interop.vimseo`)

VIMSEO (IRT Saint Exupéry; LGPL-3.0; the package `vimseo`, 0.1.7 or later, on Python 3.10
to 3.12) demonstrates the credibility of simulations — the qualification or certification
by analysis that tests support — with the tools of GEMSEO. A model of VIMSEO is a GEMSEO
discipline of named inputs and outputs (one-dimensional arrays of numbers) run for a load
case, its runs archived (the inputs, outputs and metadata of each, `results.json`) and
cached (HDF5). Its tools take such models: the verification of a code against reference
values at the same inputs, by error metrics (squared, relative, absolute errors); the
verification of a solution against its discretization, on four sizes of the elements
(Richardson's extrapolation of the output to the size zero, the observed order `β`, the
grid convergence index of Roache with the safety factor 1.25); the validation against
measurements with uncertain inputs (the area metric, the Wasserstein distance between the
distributions of the simulations and of the measurements); plans of experiments,
sensitivities, calibration.

morphoGen gives VIMSEO its computations as functions of named numbers (`Simulation`: the
defaults of the inputs, the inputs taken as whole numbers, their bounds; a variable is an
input or an output, not both, as in GEMSEO): a configuration of `morphogen run` whose
entries chosen by their dotted paths (`voxels.voxel_size`, `mesh.size`, `model.
volume_fraction`, `homogenization.materials.1.young`, `seed`; the integer keys of the
phases found as such) are the inputs and whose results of one realization (the columns
of `results.csv`; the measures asked for added to its analysis) are the outputs; and the
four Minkowski densities of the realizations of a model of spheres, exactly (§105), on the
torus of a periodic cube, the parameters of the model as inputs (prefixed `model_`, the
outputs having the names of the densities), with the closed forms of the model at the
same inputs as their references (`theory_of`): a verification of the code in which only
the fluctuation of the realizations remains. Their GEMSEO disciplines (the grammars of
one number per variable, the defaults), their VIMSEO models (`BaseDisciplineModel` of the
load case `Dummy`), the reference datasets (`IODataset`), and the two tools of
verification run on them. GEMSEO and VIMSEO are imported by these functions only.

Checked (`tests/test_vimseo.py`; with VIMSEO 0.1.7, GEMSEO 6.3.3 on Python 3.12): the
entries of nested configurations; a configuration of FFT conductivity run with its voxel
size and seed as inputs (the same seed the same outputs, another voxel size another
conductivity); the exact densities of three realizations of Boolean spheres against
their closed forms within the fluctuation of a cube of 12 (the fraction within 0.03, the
specific surface within 8 %); with VIMSEO, their code verification (relative errors
1.8 % on the fraction and 1.0 % on the specific surface over the three points) and the
solution verification of the FFT conductivity of a Boolean model (radius 1, fraction 0.3,
cube of 6) on voxels of 0.4, 0.2, 0.1 and 0.05: Richardson's extrapolation 2.278, the
observed order 0.90 (the first order of the interfaces cut by the voxels), the grid
convergence indices 7.7 % and 1.9 %.

## 113. Spinodal decomposition (`spinodal`)

A mixture quenched inside its spinodal separates into two phases by the Cahn–Hilliard
equation (Cahn & Hilliard 1958; Cahn 1961) of the composition `c` (`−1` and `1` the phases
at equilibrium), of the free energy `∫ f(c) + (κ/2)|∇c|²`, `f(c) = (c² − 1)²/4`:

    ∂c/∂t = ∇²(f'(c) − κ∇²c),        f'(c) = c³ − c

(the mobility and the scales of time and of `κ` taken as units). About the mean composition
`c̄`, inside the spinodal (`f''(c̄) = 3c̄² − 1 < 0`, `|c̄| < 1/√3`), the fluctuations of the
wave number `k` grow at the rate `ω(k) = −k²(f''(c̄) + κk²)`, the fastest at `k_m =
√(−f''/2κ)`, of the wavelength `λ_m = 2π/k_m` and the rate `ω_m = f''²/4κ`; the phases then
separate, their pattern coarsening as `t^{1/3}` (Lifshitz & Slyozov 1961; Huse 1986),
and the fraction of the phase 1 tends to the lever rule `p = (1 + c̄)/2`. The equation is
integrated on a periodic grid by the semi-implicit Fourier spectral method with a
linear stabilization `S = 2` (Chen & Shen 1998; Zhu, Chen, Shen & Tikare 1999),

    ĉ^{n+1} = (ĉ^n (1 + Δt S k²) − Δt k² F[f'(c^n)]) / (1 + Δt S k² + Δt κ k⁴),

of the steps `0.01/ω_m` at first (the linear stage resolved) growing by 2 % a step up to
`1/ω_m`; the mean composition, the mode `k = 0`, is kept exactly. The model takes the
fraction of the lever rule (0.212 to 0.788: the spinodal), the wavelength `λ_m` as the
unit of length (`resolution` points of the grid, `κ = |f''| (resolution/2π)²/2` in grid
units), the age of the pattern (`coarsening`, the time in units of `1/ω_m`) and the
amplitude of the initial fluctuations; a domain that is not periodic is a window of a
periodic box larger by a wavelength on each side. The realization is the composition on
its grid, interpolated between its points: the phase 1 is `c > 0`, its implicit function
`−c` over the median of the gradient of `c` across the interfaces, as the images of §107;
the summary gives the length `2π/k*` of the pattern from the peak `k*` of its radially
averaged structure factor.

Checked (`tests/test_spinodal.py`): on 96³ points of a symmetric mixture at the age 3,
the peak of the structure factor at `k_m = 2π/12` within a bin (0.505 for 0.524); the free
energy decreasing at every step and the mean composition kept to `10⁻¹²`; from the age 20
to the age 160 the length of the pattern doubling, `8^{1/3}`, within 10 % (2.005); the
fraction of a realization at the age 10 within 0.02 of 0.5 (0.5007), its pattern 1.19
wavelengths long; a window of an off-critical mixture (0.4); round trips.

## 114. Reconstruction from descriptors by gradient descent (`morphology.reconstruction`)

The annealing of Yeong and Torquato (§38) swaps cells one pair at a time, which keeps the
fraction and changes the two-point probability along the axes by counts of its lines; it
needs many sweeps for a large grid and sees no lag off the axes. Seibert, Ambati, Raßloff and
Kästner (2021; MCRpy, 2022) relax the indicator instead and descend the gradient of the
descriptors. On a periodic grid of $N$ cells, the field $x$ takes its values in $[0, 1]$, and

$$S_2[x](r) = \frac1N \sum_y x(y)\,x(y + r) = \frac{\mathrm{IFFT}(|\hat x|^2)(r)}{N},
\qquad \frac{\partial E}{\partial x} = \frac2N\,\mathrm{IFFT}(\hat G\,\hat x),\quad
G(r) = \frac{\partial E}{\partial S_2(r)},$$

$G$ even in $r$, at every lag of the grid at once (two transforms); its lineal path along
the axis $a$, the mean of the products $P_r(y) = \prod_{k=0}^{r} x(y + k e_a)$ — for an
indicator, the probability that $r + 1$ cells in a row lie in the phase, the lineal-path
function of §38 at the lag of $r$ cells — has the gradient
$\partial L_a(r)/\partial x(z) = \frac1N \sum_{k=0}^{r} P_r(z - k e_a)/x(z)$, the products of
the other cells of the segments through $z$, each a backward sum along the axis, $O(N)$ per
lag. The energy

$$E = \operatorname{mean}_M \frac{(S_2 - S_2^*)^2}{v^2} + \lambda_L
\operatorname{mean}_{a,r}\frac{(L_a - L_a^*)^2}{v^2} + \lambda_p \frac{(\bar x - p)^2}{v^2}
+ \mu\,\overline{x(1 - x)},$$

$v = p(1 - p)$ the variance of the indicator, $M$ the lags within the largest (a ball), is
minimized by L-BFGS-B within the bounds 0 and 1, in three stages of $\mu$ (0, 0.03, 0.3) that
draw the field to 0 and 1; the lineal paths enter after the first, the field near its
structure, and the field is thresholded at the quantile of $p$, which keeps the fraction
exactly. The bounds matter: with the field $x = \sigma(u)$ of logits $u$ instead, the factor
$x(1 - x)$ of every gradient vanishes as the cells approach 0 and 1, and the descent froze at
5 % of error on the planes of the example below, the lineal paths without effect; within the
bounds the gradient of a cell at a bound is that of its products, and a cell at 0 inside a
run of the phase is drawn back.

**Exact targets.** A model of random sets gives its descriptors in closed form, not those of
one realization with its fluctuations: the covariance $C(|r|)$ at every lag of the grid for
the isotropic models that have one (Boolean models of spheres, §1, $C = 1 - 2q +
q^2 e^{\theta E[K(h)]}$; excursions of Gaussian fields, §5) — the pores $1 - 2p + C$ — and the
lineal path of the pores of the models with a Choquet capacity,
$L_0(l) = 1 - T([0, l]) = q\,e^{-\theta\,\pi E[R^2]\,l}$ for spheres, along each axis for
oriented fibres (§2); the others are measured on a realization of the grid. An image gives
its own, interpolated at the lags of the grid; a planar image gives a volume (MCRpy's
dimensionality expansion): the section of a stationary isotropic set has the covariance of
the set at the lags of its plane, which the three coordinate planes of the grid take, and
its two lineal paths each axis of the grid. The model `reconstruction` runs it with
`method="gradient"` (`iterations`; `lineal_path` the weight $\lambda_L$).

**What the covariance does not say.** The covariance determines the fraction and the
specific surface ($S_V = -4 S_2'(0)$ in 3D, $-\pi S_2'(0)$ in 2D), not the connectivity: the
pores of plane sections of a Boolean model of spheres (radius 4 cells, 30 % of grains,
96² cells) rebuilt from their exact covariance alone match it within 0.32 % of $v$, and
miss their lineal path by 7.1 % ($L(16)$ 0.22 for 0.240); with the lineal paths among the
targets, both within 0.5 % (0.48 % and 0.44 %); for a radius of 6 cells on 160², 6.9 %
without and 0.30 % with them, $L(24)$ 0.2402 for 0.2401. In 3D (48³ cells), 6.5 % without
and 2.0 % with them ($L(12)$ 0.292 and 0.317 for 0.314), the covariance within 0.27 % and
0.67 % (35 s and 133 s for 2000 iterations).

Checked (`tests/test_gradient_reconstruction.py`): on a field of 0 and 1 the two-point
probability equals the covariance map of §38 and the lineal paths its lineal-path
function, exactly; every term of the gradient, cells at the bound 0 included, against
centred differences within $10^{-5}$; a Debye medium (§38) within 0.47 % of $v$ on 48²
cells (0.4 s) and 0.21 % on 24³ (3.7 s, 2000 iterations); the pores of sections of spheres
as above; a volume of 24³ cells from a section of 128² of a Boolean model of spheres
(radius 3 cells): the planes within 0.43 %, and the lags off them within 3.5 % of the exact
3D covariance (on 40³ from a section of 192², radius 4: 0.50 % and 2.4 %) — closer than a
realization of the model itself on 40³ (18 %: its fluctuation); the model with
`method="gradient"` from the closed forms of a reference, a Debye medium and an image,
their errors within 2 %, and its round trip.

## 115. Grains grown from seeds (`models.seeded`, `kernels.seeds`)

The cells of a Laguerre tessellation are convex polyhedra, and the tessellation of the germs
of a packing of spheres (§4) gives grains of the sizes of the spheres, not of chosen shapes.
MicroStructPy (Hart & Rimoli 2020a, 2020b) grows the grains from seeds of any shape
instead: each seed is broken down into spheres, the spheres of all the seeds are the germs
of one Laguerre tessellation, their weights the squares of their radii, and the grain of a
seed is the union of the cells of its spheres — not convex in general, its shape that of
its seed where the seeds fill the box. The model `seeded_laguerre` grows them from
ellipsoidal seeds.

**The seeds.** A seed has an equivalent diameter $d$ (that of the sphere of its volume) and
the ratios $a/b \ge 1$ and $b/c \ge 1$ of its semi-axes, each drawn from its law, so that
$c = \tfrac d2\,[(a/b)(b/c)^2]^{-1/3}$ and $abc = (d/2)^3$. The seeds are drawn until their
volumes $\pi d^3/6$ fill the box (a box that is not periodic dilated by the largest diameter,
so that its faces cut grains), their axes turned by uniform rotations or aligned with those
of the box, their phases drawn with the fractions of the phases.

**Breakdown.** The ellipsoid $x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 + z^2/c^2 \le 1$ ($a \ge b \ge c$) holds, about
each point of its medial surface — the ellipse of semi-axes $(a^2 - c^2)/a$ and
$(b^2 - c^2)/b$ in the plane $z = 0$, a segment for a prolate spheroid — a largest sphere,
which touches it at the nearest points of its surface: from $(x, y, 0)$ they are
$(a^2 x/(a^2 - c^2),\, b^2 y/(b^2 - c^2),\, \pm z)$, where the normal points back to the
centre, which gives its radius in closed form ($c$ at the centre, the radius of curvature
$c^2/a$ at the ends of the long axis). The spheres are centred on a triangular lattice of the
medial ellipse and on its rim, at the spacing `spacing` times $c$ (widened to keep at most
256 spheres per seed); their union fills the ellipsoid as follows (Monte Carlo):

| Semi-axes $a, b, c$ | Spacing 0.25 | 0.5 (default) | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2, 1, 1 | 13 spheres, 99.0 % | 7, 95.9 % | 4, 83.3 % |
| 4, 1, 1 | 31, 99.2 % | 16, 96.7 % | 9, 88.3 % |
| 2, 2, 1 | 161, 98.4 % | 52, 94.3 % | 17, 80.5 % |
| 3, 2, 1 | 284, 98.6 % | 88, 95.0 % | 27, 80.1 % |
| 6, 3, 1 | 1014, 98.7 % | 283, 94.8 % | 84, 79.7 % |

MicroStructPy approximates the elliptical sections $x$–$z$ and $y$–$z$ of the seed by circles
and scales them into spheres; here each sphere is inscribed in the seed and touches it.

**Placement.** The seeds are placed the largest first, each at the first of uniform positions
where its spheres overlap those of the seeds already placed by at most a tolerance $t$: for
every sphere $k$ of the seed at $c$ (its centre $c + o_k$) and every sphere $q$ placed,
$|c + o_k - x_q| + t \min(r_k, r_q) \ge r_k + r_q$ — the depth of their overlap at most $t$
times the smaller radius (0: none; 1: the centre of the smaller on the surface of the
other), across the faces of a periodic box. The default tolerance is the rational fit of
MicroStructPy, in 3D, to the tolerances that Hart and Rimoli (2020a) plot against the coefficient of
variation $v$ of the volumes of the seeds (their Fig. 10),

$$t(v) = \frac{0.471115\,v^2 - 0.602324\,v + 0.297562}{v^2 - 1.08469\,v + 0.428216},$$

0.695 for seeds of one size, 0.86 at $v = 0.4$, 0.48 at $v = 1$ (the default of `overlap`).
The positions are drawn 32 per seed for 64 seeds at a time, and the rest of its attempts
(10 000 in all, as MicroStructPy) for a seed that clears at none of them; the spheres placed
are kept in grids by levels of sizes (§116), so that a position is tested against the
spheres within reach, its test stopping as soon as its overlap exceeds the least found so
far for the seed.

**Crowded seeds.** The sequential addition of elongated seeds jams before they fill the box.
MicroStructPy leaves out a seed that clears at none of its positions, its volume going to the
grains of its neighbours, larger than their seeds. Here it is placed at the position of its
least excess of overlap, $\max_{k,q} (r_k + r_q - |c + o_k - x_q|)/\min(r_k, r_q) - t$, by
default (`crowded: place`): every seed has its grain, of its volume on average;
`crowded: leave` leaves it out.

**The grains.** A point belongs to the sphere of least power distance $|x - x_k|^2 - r_k^2$
(the k-d tree of the tessellation, exact at any point) and to the grain of its seed
(`SeededTessellation`: the labels of the grains, `grain_of`, their exact volumes from the
cells, their phases and crystal orientations, the table of their seeds). The implicit
function of a phase takes the distance to the faces between the cells of different grains:
the distance to the boundary of the grain where the cell of the point holds its nearest
part, a lower bound otherwise, its sign exact. The conforming mesh of a polycrystal (§19)
merges the cells of each grain in the complex of the cells (`CellComplex.merged`): the facets
between them are no longer between cells, MMG meshes the grain as one subdomain, its
elements with the phase and the orientation of the grain. With the exact facets of whole
periodic cells (§24), MMG did not end with the merged grains (more than 300 s for 6 grains
of 42 spheres, which their cells cut by the box mesh in 3 s): those are meshed cell by cell,
then relabelled by grain (2 s), their volumes exact to $10^{-14}$. The surfaces of the cells are
drawn grain by grain, and the elements of the crack meshes of a polycrystal take the grains
of their centroids. The tessellations of Neper, of convex cells, do not describe them: its
export refuses them.

**Against MicroStructPy.** MicroStructPy 1.6.1 and morphoGen on the same seeds: a periodic
cube of edge 6, seeds of equivalent diameter 1 (413 of them), the tolerance of the fit
(0.695). Spheres: all placed by both, the grains of the volumes of their seeds on average
(0.999), the coefficient of variation of their volumes 0.147 (MicroStructPy 0.150). Seeds of
aspect ratio 3 at random: MicroStructPy keeps 276 of them (its positioning 375 s), its
grains 1.495 times the volume of their seeds on average, the coefficient of variation of
their volumes 0.108; morphoGen keeps 276 of them too with `crowded: leave` (1.5 s; 1.495 and
0.104), and with `crowded: place` all of them (156 crowded) in 2.0 s, the grains of the
volumes of their seeds (0.999; 0.148). The shapes of the grains, from the second moments of
their labels (120³ voxels, the coordinates about their seeds), medians: seeds of aspect
ratio 3, the grains $a/b$ 3.08 and $b/c$ 1.16, their long axes along those of their seeds
($|\cos|$ 0.999) — 2.77 when the crowded seeds are left out, their grains swollen by the
volume of the others —; seeds of ratios $a/b = b/c = 2$, the grains 2.11 and 2.08 ($|\cos|$
0.998; 118 spheres a seed, 48 734 in all, 241 seeds crowded, placed in 69 s); spheres, 1.14
and 1.15 (the facets of the cells), their axes at random.

Checked (`tests/test_seeded_grains.py`): each sphere of the breakdown of five ellipsoids
touches it at the nearest points in closed form (on the surface within $10^{-12}$, at the
distance of its radius, the normal through its centre) and no point of a sampling of 180 000
points of the surface is nearer; their union at least 93 % of the ellipsoid at the spacing
0.5 and 97 % at 0.25; the fit of the tolerance at three variations; seeds of one sphere and
of two placed in a periodic box within the tolerance, those of a box too small left out or
placed crowded, the seeds that clear within the tolerance of each other; seeds of one size:
one grain per seed, the volumes of the grains summing to that of the box (to $10^{-9}$) and
their mean that of the seeds (2 %), in a box that is not periodic too; seeds of aspect ratio
2.5 at random give grains of ratio 2 to 3 along their seeds' axes ($|\cos|$ > 0.98), flat
seeds flat grains; elongated seeds placed crowded or left out; the parameters checked, the
labels those of the grains, the realization saved and read back, the table, the export to
Neper refused; the exact surfaces by grain, their regions the grains with their phases; the
elements of a mesh in the grains of their centroids; the mesh of the grains, their volumes
those of the grains within 2 %, their phases and orientations, and with the exact facets of
whole and cut cells to $10^{-9}$.

## 116. Seeds of several phases and the verification of their grains (`models.seeded`, `mesh.polyhedra`, `kernels.seeds`)

**Phases of their own seeds.** MicroStructPy describes each phase by its fraction of the
volume, the laws of its seeds and its kind (crystalline, amorphous, void). `seeded_laguerre`
takes the laws of each phase (`phase_diameter`, `phase_aspect_ratio`, `phase_flatness`,
`phase_orientation`, instead of the shared ones). MicroStructPy draws the phase of each
seed at random, the phase $i$ with the probability

$$p_i = \frac{q_i / E[V_i]}{\sum_j q_j / E[V_j]},\qquad E[V_i] = \frac\pi6 E[d_i^3],$$

so that the seeds of each phase fill its fraction $q_i$ of the volume in expectation; here
the seeds of each phase are drawn until they fill it (§118: the fractions of the seeds exact
to a seed), the mean volume of the seeds $1/\sum_i q_i/E[V_i]$; the seeds of all the phases
are placed together, the largest first. The template `seeded_matrix` (a glass of seeds of
diameter 0.08, laths of 0.22 and of ratio 3, equiaxed crystals of 0.16, in the fractions 0.4,
0.4 and 0.2) gives 0.397 to 0.402, 0.396 to 0.403 and 0.200 to 0.202 in three periodic cubes
of edge 1 (about 1650 seeds), 0.402, 0.398 and 0.200 in a cube of edge 2 (13 224 seeds);
with the phases of the seeds drawn at random, 0.353 to 0.386 for the glass in cubes of edge
1, the fluctuation of some seventy laths.

**Amorphous phases.** The seeds of an amorphous phase (`amorphous_phases`) are merged into
one region: the cells of their spheres make a single grain — one label, no grain boundary
inside, no seed of its own (its row of the table NaN, `null` in the files), the identity
orientation —, the grains of the other phases being crystals, one per seed. The distance to
the grain boundaries inside the region is that to the crystals: the faces between its cells
are no boundaries (a lower bound, its sign exact, §115). A void is an amorphous phase that
the meshes leave out: the mesh of the polycrystal keeps the phases it is given
(`phases: [1, 2]`), the region of the matrix one subdomain otherwise.

**The exact shapes of the grains.** The cells are convex polyhedra. A tetrahedron
$(0, a, b, c)$ has the volume $V = \det[a, b, c]/6$, the first moment $V(a + b + c)/4$ and
the second moment $\frac{V}{20}(aa^T + bb^T + cc^T + ss^T)$, $s = a + b + c$; summed over the
fans of the facets of a piece from one of its vertices, signed by the orientation of the
facets, they give its volume, centroid and central second moment exactly
(`CellComplex.piece_moments`: the pieces of a tessellation of a box sum to the moments of the
box within $10^{-12}$). A grain gathers its pieces — in a periodic box its whole cells, each
translated next to its first one — by the parallel-axis theorem, and the ellipsoid of the
same second moments has the semi-axes $\sqrt{5\lambda_i}$, $\lambda_i$ the eigenvalues of
the covariance $S/V$ (a solid ellipsoid of semi-axes $a, b, c$ has the covariance
$\mathrm{diag}(a^2, b^2, c^2)/5$), along their eigenvectors (`Tessellation.grain_shapes`, for
any tessellation; the grains cut by the faces of a box that is not periodic marked).

**The grains against their seeds.** MicroStructPy fits a geometry to the points of the
faces of each grain of its mesh and compares the outputs with the inputs: the errors seed by
seed (mean absolute, mean square and largest errors, $R^2$) and the distributions of the
grains against the laws of the seeds (Wasserstein, energy, Kolmogorov–Smirnov, t). Here
`SeededTessellation.seed_comparison` compares the seed of each crystal with the ellipsoid
of its grain — the equivalent diameter, the ratios $a/b$ and $b/c$, the angle between their
distinguished axes (the long one, or the short one of a flat seed) —: the bias, the mean
absolute, RMS and largest errors, $R^2 = 1 - \mathrm{MSE}/\mathrm{var}$ (of the grains; for
seeds of one size it measures nothing), and the Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance
$\sup |F_n - F|$ of the grains of each phase to the law of its seeds (a continuous law, the
distribution functions in closed form, `Distribution.cdf`); and the fractions of the
phases, realized and asked. The named measure `exact_grains` gives them as columns of a run:
the number of grains, the mean and the coefficient of variation of their diameters, the
medians of their ratios, the fractions of the phases; the relative RMS error of the
diameters, the RMS errors of the ratios, the mean angle, the largest distance of
Kolmogorov–Smirnov.

Periodic cubes, seed 1: seeds of one sphere (edge 4, 123 grains), the diameters of the grains
within 5.6 % RMS of those of their seeds, their ellipsoids of ratios 1.15 (the facets of the
cells); seeds of aspect ratio 3 at random (edge 6, 413 grains), the diameters within 5.0 %,
the ratios $a/b$ within 0.36 RMS (a bias of +0.12), the long axes 2.9° from those of their
seeds on average and 7.6° at most; lognormal diameters (coefficient of variation 0.2) and
$a/b$ uniform on $[1.5, 2.5]$ (edge 5, 228 grains), $R^2$ 0.977 for the diameters, the
distances of Kolmogorov–Smirnov 0.083 and 0.091 (the critical value at 5 % is 0.090 for 228
grains: the ratios at its edge); the crystals of the template `seeded_matrix` (seed 2), their
diameters within 1.0 %, their ratios within 0.050, their axes within 0.68°: the small seeds
of the glass, placed last, fill around the crystals without deforming them.

**Seeds of very different sizes.** One grid of cells of twice the largest radius (§115) puts
every sphere of a matrix of small seeds in the 27 cells about a candidate. The levels
$l = 0, 1, \dots$ hold the spheres of radii up to $r_{max}/2^l$ in cells at least
$2 r_{max}/2^l$ wide (at most 8 levels of $2^{22}$ cells); a sphere of radius $r$ meets
those of the level $l$ within $\lceil (r + r_l)/h_l \rceil$ cells of its own, $r_l$ the
largest radius placed there (the empty levels skipped). The search starts at the level of
the sphere, then the coarser and the finer ones, from its own cell outwards — the overlaps
that end a test, its excess beyond the least found, are with the spheres of its size about
it —, and the spheres of a seed the largest first. The placements are those of the single
grid, in: three phases (a glass of seeds of 0.08, laths of 0.25 on average and crystals of
0.2, 1509 seeds), 31.6 s before and 5.3 s after; seeds of aspect ratio 3, 3.7 s and 1.9 s;
the template `seeded_matrix` in a cube of edge 2 (13 154 seeds, 4634 of them crowded), 96 s
and 34 s — the seeds of the glass, placed last into a full box, try their 10 000 positions
each, and fewer `attempts` make them faster.

Checked (`tests/test_seeded_phases.py`, `tests/test_polydispersity.py`): the distribution
functions of the five laws against 40 000 draws (within 0.01) and against their quadratures,
the distance of Kolmogorov–Smirnov that of SciPy; the moments of the cells of a box that is
not periodic summing to those of the box (to $10^{-12}$), their volumes those of the cell
complex; the cell of a single germ, the box, of semi-axes $\sqrt{5/12}\,L$; the grains of a
periodic tessellation filling the box, those cut by the faces of a box marked; seeds of
lognormal diameters and uniform ratios against their grains (the diameters within 5 % RMS,
the ratios within 0.3, the axes within 10°, $R^2$ above 0.9, Kolmogorov–Smirnov below 0.15),
the columns of `exact_grains`; two phases of their own sizes, their shares, fractions
(within 0.08) and diameters, aligned seeds, the parameters checked; an amorphous matrix, one
region without a seed and with the identity orientation, the distance to the crystals inside
it (beyond the faces of its cells for a fifth of the points at least, a lower bound of the
distance to them), saved without NaN and read back, meshed as one subdomain or left out;
seeds of radii 0.02 to 0.6 placed in boxes periodic or not, the seeds that clear within the
tolerance of those before them by brute force.

## 117. Seeds of the plane and the figures of the verification (`models.seeded`, `viz.figures`)

**Seeds of the plane.** MicroStructPy grows microstructures of the plane from ellipses.
`seeded_laguerre` with `dimension: 2` draws elliptical seeds in the middle plane $z$ of the
box: their equivalent diameter $d$ is that of the disc of their area, $\pi a b = \pi d^2/4$,
with their ratio $a/b$ and their long axis at a uniform angle in the plane or along $x$
(`aligned`); they fill the area of the box, the seeds of each phase with
$p_i \propto q_i/E[A_i]$, $E[A_i] = \pi E[d_i^2]/4$. An ellipse is broken down as the
section through its axis of the prolate spheroid $(a, b, b)$: the circles centred on its
medial segment $|x| \le (a^2 - b^2)/a$, each the largest of the ellipse about its centre
(§115: the spheres of the spheroid cut by the plane), at the spacing $0.5\,b$. The
positions tried lie in the middle plane (the kernel draws $x$ and $y$), and the tolerance
is the fit of MicroStructPy in the plane,

$$t(v) = \frac{0.362954\,v^2 - 0.419069\,v + 0.184959}{v^2 - 1.05989\,v + 0.365096},$$

0.507 for seeds of one size, $v$ the coefficient of variation of their areas. With all the
germs in one plane, the power distance of a point $(x, y, z)$ to a germ $(x_k, y_k, z_0)$ is
that of the plane plus $(z - z_0)^2$, the same for every germ: the Laguerre cells are the
prisms of the power diagram of the circles in the plane through the thickness — in a
periodic box too, the images of the germs in $z$ being no nearer — and the grains are
columnar, the same labels on every layer of voxels. A box that is not periodic is widened in
the plane only.

**Their verification.** The grains of the plane are measured by their sections: the area
$V/L_z$ of each, the diameter of the disc of that area and the ellipse of the same second
moments in the plane, the covariance of a solid ellipse being $\mathrm{diag}(a^2, b^2)/4$
(`grain_shapes`, two semi-axes); `seed_comparison` and `exact_grains` compare the diameters,
the ratios $a/b$ and the long axes. Seeds of lognormal diameters (coefficient of variation
0.2) and of $a/b$ uniform on $[1.5, 3]$ in a periodic square of edge 12 (184 grains): the
diameters within 6.7 % RMS ($R^2$ 0.925, Kolmogorov–Smirnov 0.083), the long axes 3.5°
from those of their seeds on average. The ratios of the grains exceed those of their seeds
(a bias of +0.42, Kolmogorov–Smirnov 0.26): a cell of a partition is no ellipse, and discs
give grains whose ellipses have the ratio 1.31 on average (1.15 for the grains of spheres in
space), seeds of the ratio 2 grains of 2.37. The template `seeded_plane` (the section of a
rolled sheet: grains of lognormal sizes and of $a/b$ uniform on $[2, 3.5]$ along $x$, among
the equiaxed grains of a second phase, 0.8 and 0.2 of the area) gives the fractions 0.814
and 0.186, the diameters within 7.0 %, the axes within 2.0°, the distances of
Kolmogorov–Smirnov 0.070 and 0.097 (138 grains, 6 s).

**The figures.** `seed_figure` draws what MicroStructPy draws after its verification: for
each quantity the distribution functions of the grains of each phase (solid), of their seeds
(dotted) and the law of the seeds of the phase (black, `Distribution.cdf`), on the bulk of
the values (to 1.1 times the 98th percentile of the grains: a few slivers do not stretch the
axis); the histogram of the angles between the axes of the grains and of their seeds; the
fractions of the phases, asked and realized. The tool *Grains and their seeds* of the
interface (Statistics) gives the tables of the errors and of the fractions and this figure
for a realization of `seeded_laguerre` of the workspace (the trait `seeds` of its items).

Checked (`tests/test_seeded_phases.py`, `tests/test_gui_tools.py`): elliptical seeds in the
middle plane of a thin periodic box, the germs in that plane, the tolerance of the plane for
seeds of one size, the same labels on four layers, the areas of the grains summing to that
of the box, two semi-axes and no ratio b/c, the diameters within 8 % RMS and the axes within
8°, the columns of `exact_grains`, the number of grains within 15 % of the theory; in a box
that is not periodic, the seeds about it in the plane only and the grains cut by its sides,
not by its faces $z$; the parameters checked; the figure, five panels for two phases in
space and four in the plane; the tool, the trait of the items grown from seeds, its tables
and its figure, a polycrystal of germs refused.

## 118. Seeds of boxes and of rectangles (`models.seeded`)

**Shapes.** MicroStructPy approximates rectangles and squares by circles — a row along
the long axis and chains of smaller circles towards the corners — but has no breakdown of
boxes. `shape: box` (per phase, `phase_shape`) makes the seeds boxes of the half sides
$a \ge b \ge c$ in the ratios $a/b$ and $b/c$ (rectangles in the plane), of the volume of the
sphere of their equivalent diameter, $8abc = \pi d^3/6$ ($4ab = \pi d^2/4$ in the plane).

**Breakdown.** The largest sphere inscribed in a box about a point has the radius of its
least distance to the faces. Those of the radius $c$ fill the slab about the medial rectangle
$|x| \le a - c$, $|y| \le b - c$ of the box (on a lattice of the spacing $0.5\,c$): all of
it but a rounding of the radius $c$ along its edges. A sphere of a radius $r < c$ touching
the two faces of an edge has its centre on the edge of the box eroded by $r$: at the levels
$k = 1, 2$, $r = c/2^k$, spheres along the twelve edges of the eroded boxes (at the spacing
$k\,r$) fill those roundings down to that of the radius $c/4$; the spheres within larger ones
are dropped, and the spacings widen to keep 256 spheres at most (`box_spheres`). They fill
(Monte Carlo) a cube with 53 spheres at 87.7 %, the boxes $(2, 1, 1)$ with 89 at 90.4 %,
$(2, 1.5, 1)$ with 115 at 91.9 %, $(3, 2, 1)$ with 193 at 93.6 %, $(4, 2, 0.5)$ with 238 at
85.6 % (the spacings widened). A rectangle takes the circles of the radius $b$ on its medial
segment $|x| \le a - b$ and, at the levels $k = 1, 2, 3$, one of the radius $b/2^k$ at each
corner of the rectangle eroded by it (the chains of corners of MicroStructPy): 98 to 99 % of
it with 13 to 29 circles.

**The grains.** The ellipsoid of the same second moments as a box of half sides $a, b, c$
has the semi-axes $\sqrt{5/3}\,(a, b, c)$, in the ratios of the box: `seed_comparison`
compares the ratios of the boxes with those of their grains, and the diameters with those of
the volumes of the seeds, kept with them. Periodic cubes, seed 1, the equivalent diameter 1:
cubes aligned with the box (edge 4, 123 grains, 6519 spheres), the diameters of the grains
within 7.2 % RMS of their seeds, their ellipsoids of the ratios 1.13 and 1.12 (those of the
cells of spheres 1.15); boxes of the ratios 2 and 1.5 at random (edge 4, 123 grains, 19 557
spheres, placed in 16 s, verified in 135 s), within 8.7 %, the ratios 1.86 and 1.51, the axes
7.0° from those of their seeds. In the plane (squares of edge 10), rectangles of the ratio 2
along $x$, 19.1 % (the ratio 1.97, the axes within 7.5°); squares at random, 15.5 % (the
ratio 1.30); ellipses of the ratio 2 along $x$, 7.3 % (2.31; 4.4°). Polygonal seeds jam the
sequential addition sooner — 43 % of the rectangles crowded for 27 % of the ellipses, the
small circles of their corners counting their overlaps in their own radii — and their grains
deviate more; left out (`crowded: leave`), 54 of the 128 rectangles, the grains of the
others 32.7 % from their seeds. The template `seeded_precipitates` (the cubes of γ′ of a
nickel superalloy aligned with the box, of lognormal diameters about 0.4, 0.6 of the volume,
in a matrix of seeds of 0.12 merged into one region) gives 62 cubes within 1.7 % RMS of their
seeds (a bias of −0.3 %), of the ratios 1.03 and 1.02, and the fractions 0.592 and 0.408: the
small seeds of the matrix, placed last, fill around the cubes without deforming them.

**Phases filled.** The seeds of each phase are drawn until their volumes fill its fraction
of the volume: $q_i V / E[V_i]$ of them on average — the shares $p_i \propto q_i / E[V_i]$
with which MicroStructPy draws the phase of each seed at random —, the fractions of the seeds
then exact to a seed, where phases drawn at random fluctuate: for the template
`seeded_precipitates`, 0.559 and 0.610 of precipitates in two realizations with the phases at
random, 0.604 to 0.607 in four filled (their grains 0.583 to 0.593).

Checked (`tests/test_seeded_phases.py`): the spheres of a cube and of the boxes $(2, 1, 1)$
and $(3, 2, 1)$ inside them and filling 87 % of them at least, 256 at most, the circles of
rectangles 97 % of them; cubes aligned with the box, their half sides and volumes, their
grains of their volumes within 8 % RMS; rectangles of the ratio 2 along $x$, their grains
of ratios 1.6 to 2.6 along their seeds (within 8°); boxes and ellipsoids of two phases, the
table of the volumes of the seeds; the parameters checked.

## 119. Meshes of the plane and their finite elements (`mesh.triangles`, `homogenization.plane`)

**Structures of the plane.** A structure invariant along $z$ — the columnar grains of a
tessellation whose germs lie in one plane (the seeds of the plane of §117), the section of
long fibres, a layer whose fields do not vary through its thickness — is meshed in its plane
by triangles (`TriMesh`: three- or six-node elements counterclockwise, a phase each, a grain
each with the orientations of the grains, the rectangle of the box, its periodicity, the
height $z$ of the plane and the thickness of the box). The mesher in space cannot take such a
tessellation: its cells are prisms through the whole thickness of the box, and its facets
across the faces $z$ are the cells themselves.

**Exact polygons.** With all the germs in one plane, the cell of a germ is the prism of its
cell in the power diagram of the plane, the points of least power distance
$|x - x_k|^2 - w_k$. The cell of germ $i$ is the polygon cut from a rectangle about the box
by the half planes of its neighbours $j$,

$$(x_j - x_i)\cdot x \le \tfrac12\,(|x_j|^2 - |x_i|^2 - w_j + w_i),$$

clipped one after the other (Sutherland and Hodgman), the neighbours taken from a k-d tree
of the germs and of their eight periodic images until the farthest of them lies beyond
$\rho + \sqrt{\rho^2 - w_i + w_{\max}}$, $\rho$ the reach of the polygon from its germ — no
farther germ can cut it. In a periodic box, the polygon and its eight translates are cut by
the box; the vertices of the pieces are merged within $10^{-9}$ of the box
(`planar_pieces`). The areas of the pieces are those of the exact cells in space over the
thickness (`grain_shapes`) to $3 \cdot 10^{-14}$.

**Edges graded from the small features.** The edges between grains and those of the sides are
subdivided, then kept as they are while `mmg2d` remeshes the grains (`-nosurf`): left to
`mmg2d`, the interfaces would follow its smooth curves through the corners of the polygons
(the nodes of the boundaries 6·10⁻³ off the polygons, the areas of the grains 0.8 % off).
The grain boundaries of seeds are polylines of short edges (those of the cells of the spheres
of two seeds), and an edge subdivided at the size of the elements next to an edge of 10⁻⁴
gives slivers (angles of 0.04°). The edges are subdivided at a size field

$$h(x) = \min\Big(h_{\max},\ \min_k\,\big(h_k + g\,|x - p_k|\big)\Big), \qquad g = 0.25,$$

over points $p_k$ along the edges every $h_{\max}/4$, whose sizes $h_k$ are their distances to
the nearest edge that does not touch theirs (thin grains, close corners; across the sides of
a periodic box with the vertices of the sides identified with their translates), at most the
lengths of the edges of the vertices among them: the elements grow by at most a quarter from
one to the next away from the small features. Each edge is marched from one end at the sizes
of the field and its steps scaled to end on the other; the edges of the upper sides of a
periodic box are the translates of those of the lower sides, and the opposite sides match
node for node. The 46 grains of seeds of the plane in a periodic square of edge 6
(`size: 0.2`) are meshed by 15 138 triangles in 0.4 s, their areas within 6·10⁻¹⁴ of those of
the exact grains and the smallest angle 7.7°; in a box that is not periodic, 59 grains in
17 391 triangles (6.5°); the 400 cells of a periodic Voronoi mosaic (edge 10, `size: 0.1`) in
38 658 triangles in 0.6 s (5.3°).

**The small features.** The exact polygons of the plane have small features: the short edges
where the cells of the spheres of two seeds meet along a grain boundary, and the thin caps of
the cells that the box cuts near its sides — wedges whose elements are flat whatever their
grading (a cap 10⁻⁶ thick gives angles of 0°). As the cells in space (§10), the features
smaller than `min_feature` (by default a quarter of the size; 0 keeps the exact polygons)
are removed before meshing: the edges between grains or on the sides shorter than it
collapse, their ends merged on the torus of a periodic box (the copies of a vertex on
opposite sides alike, on the side or the corner of a vertex of one); the vertices nearer
than it to a side move onto it, or onto the vertex of the side nearer than it (no short edge
along the sides); the loops lose the vertices where they then turn back along
a side, the pieces left without area vanish, and the vertices of the sides of a periodic box
get their translates on the opposite sides, inserted in the edges there — the sides match,
and the areas sum to the box. The grains of the template `seeded_plane_stiffness` (90 grains
of seeds elongated along $x$ in the unit square, `size: 0.025`, four realizations): 52 000 to
59 000 triangles with the exact polygons, the smallest angles 0 to 9°; 8 200 to 8 500
regularized, the smallest angles 7.7 to 11.1°, the areas of the grains within 0.4 to 0.6 %
of the exact ones on average (2 to 4 % at most). A piece that the regularization leaves not
star-shaped about its centroid is cut into triangles by ear clipping; where the polygons
would fold, the features are removed at half the size, three times at most, before the exact
polygons.

**Sections.** Any other structure is meshed in its plane $z$ from the implicit functions of its
phases (`section_mesh`), as in space (§11): sampled at the nodes of a triangulation of the
rectangle (a grid of squares cut by diagonals that alternate with their parity, symmetric
about the lines of the grid), the values near zero moved away from it, the phases cut one
after another by the level sets of `mmg2d` (its multi-material references, the phases cut
before left whole), then remeshed within the Hausdorff distance of the interfaces, the sides
of a periodic structure kept as the cut left them — matching, the functions taking the same
values on opposite sides.

**Curved edges.** The six-node triangles of a section have their nodes of the interfaces on
the curves of the section (`curved_triangles`, by default; `curved: false` keeps the straight
edges of the mesher), as the ten-node tetrahedra in space (§76). The nodes of an edge between
the phases $a$ and $b$ go to the zero of $\varphi_a - \varphi_b$ (of $\varphi_a$ for the wall
of a pore left out of the mesh) along its gradient in the plane, by Newton's method; those of
the sides of the box along the sides, those of opposite sides of a periodic mesh alike; the
nodes where three phases meet stay. The corners move first, by at most 0.3 of their shortest
edge and as far as their straight triangles keep half of their areas and of their qualities,
in three steps; then the middle nodes, by at most 0.3 of their edges and as far as the area
element of each curved triangle keeps 0.3 of that of its straight triangle at its six nodes
and its three integration points. An element is its straight triangle moved by
$\sum_k N_k d_k$, $d_k$ the departures of its middle nodes from the middles of its edges:
its gradients are those of the straight triangle times $F^{-1}$,
$F = I + \sum_k d_k \otimes \nabla N_k$, and its weights times $\det F$ — a polynomial of
the second degree, so that the three integration points give its area exactly. The
structures that give their functions at any point (the unions of spheres and segments, their
coatings, the long fibres) have their nodes put on their curves exactly, the others on the
cubic splines of their functions sampled on a grid of the plane at an eighth of the size of
the elements. The layer in space of curved triangles (`TriMesh.layer`) has the middle nodes
of its edges over the curved edges where those of the triangles are, at their heights: its
faces are the curved edges extruded, the volumes of its phases their areas times its
thickness exactly, its fields independent of $z$ those of the triangles, and its tensors those
of the plane but for the integration points, which differ on curved elements (5·10⁻⁷ for a
coated cylinder meshed at the size 0.15). Checked, on the meshes of their level sets
(`section_mesh`; by their circles below): the fibres of a square array filling 0.4 of
the plane have their area within 9.5·10⁻⁷ at the size 0.1 and 7.3·10⁻⁸ at 0.05 (4·10⁻³ and
2·10⁻³ off with straight edges), the fourth power of the size, and within 3·10⁻⁶ on the
splines of their sampled functions; their conductivity against the series of Perrins,
McKenzie & McPhedran (1979), ten times as conducting as the matrix, within 3.1·10⁻⁵ at the
size 0.1 and 1.2·10⁻⁵ at 0.05 (1.4·10⁻³ off with straight edges), insulating, their walls
curved, within 4.0·10⁻⁵ and 4·10⁻⁶; at the fraction 0.6, where the series is 5·10⁻⁴ off, the
reciprocal theorem of Keller (1964), $\sigma(1, t)\,\sigma(1, 1/t) = 1$ for the ratio $t = 10$,
holds within 6.9·10⁻⁵, 6.2·10⁻⁶ and 6.8·10⁻⁷ at the sizes 0.1, 0.05 and 0.025. A coated
cylinder is neutral (Hashin & Rosen 1964) in a matrix of the conductivity
$\sigma_s\,((1+c)\,\sigma_c + (1-c)\,\sigma_s)/((1-c)\,\sigma_c + (1+c)\,\sigma_s)$ and of the
plane bulk modulus $k_s + c/(1/(k_c - k_s) + (1-c)/(k_s + \mu_s))$ ($c$ the share of the core
in the coated cylinder, $k = \lambda + \mu$): the field about it stays uniform, and the cell
has them under any condition — within 1.5·10⁻⁵ and 6·10⁻⁶ at the size 0.1 and 5·10⁻⁷ and
2·10⁻⁷ at 0.025, under the kinematic, periodic and static conditions alike (10⁻³ and 3·10⁻⁴
off with straight edges).

**Exact discs.** The sections of the straight fibres along $z$ of a union of segments (the
long fibres without misalignment) and those of spheres are discs (`disc_sections`: the cuts
by the plane, of radii $\sqrt{r^2 - d^2}$ at the distance $d$ of the plane from a centre, or
from the axis of a segment beyond its end; the periodic images along $z$ taken, the
concentric discs of the segments of one fibre merged). Those that do not meet are meshed by
their circles (`disc_mesh`, by default for them in `plane_mesh`): each circle discretized
exactly — its nodes on it —, by 24 segments at least and at sizes graded from the gaps,
$h(x) = \min(h_{\max}, \min_k (h_k + g\,|x - p_k|))$ over points $p_k$ of the circles and of the
sides whose sizes $h_k$ are a third of their gaps to the nearest other circle (and to the
sides that a circle does not cross), $h_{\max}/64$ at least: three elements across the
narrowest gap. The points where the circles cross the sides of the box are those of their
images on the opposite sides, the nodes of the upper sides the translates of those of the
lower sides; `mmg2d` meshes the regions within these edges, which it keeps (`-nosurf`), and
each triangle takes the phase of its centroid. The six-node elements have only their middle
nodes to move onto the circles. Coated fibres and spheres, and hollow ones (the model
`coating`, outside or inside), are rings: their concentric circles (`disc_layers`; the cuts
of the members grown by the thickness of the coating, or shrunk by that of the shells), the
band of each centroid giving its phase, and the coatings graded too — three elements across
them. Plain discs that cross each other — the sections of a Boolean model of fibres along
$z$ or of spheres: a Boolean model of discs — are meshed by the boundary of their union. The
circles of two discs at the distance $d$ cross at $c_i + a\,u \pm \sqrt{r_i^2 - a^2}\,u^\perp$,
$u$ the unit vector from $c_i$ to $c_j$ and $a = (r_i^2 - r_j^2 + d^2)/2d$: the corners of the
union where they lie outside the other discs, nodes of both circles. The arcs between the
crossings of a circle with the others and with the sides are kept where their middles lie
outside the other discs, a disc inside another is left out, and the gaps are graded between
the circles that do not cross; the sizes at the corners of the union, where the fields are
singular, are an eighth of what they would be (`CORNER_REFINEMENT`). Discs that touch,
outside or inside, coatings that meet and oblique fibres are left to the level sets. Two fibres of radius 0.2 whose axes are 0.3 apart
have the area of their union, two discs less their lens $2r^2\arccos(d/2r) -
\tfrac{d}{2}\sqrt{4r^2 - d^2}$, within 4.3·10⁻⁶, 3.7·10⁻⁷ and 2.5·10⁻⁸ at the sizes 0.05,
0.025 and 0.0125: the fourth power of the size, the corners of the union nodes (6.2·10⁻³,
1.9·10⁻³ and 5.1·10⁻⁴ off with the chords). Boolean cylinders of radius 0.06 along $z$
filling 0.4 of a periodic cube, cut by its middle plane in 50 discs that cross each other or
their images 107 times, are meshed in 0.6 s at the size 0.04 by 15 860 triangles, the area of
their union within 4·10⁻⁶ of its count on a grid of 4000² points, the precision of the count
(2.1·10⁻³ off with the chords). The reciprocal theorem of Keller, in the form Mendelson
(1975) gave it for the tensors of any microstructure of two phases in the plane,
$K(t)\,R\,K(1/t)\,R^{\mathsf T} = I$ with $R$ the quarter turn, holds there within
4.4·10⁻⁴, 2.2·10⁻⁴ and 9·10⁻⁵ at the sizes 0.04, 0.02 and 0.01; without the grading toward
the corners, 6 940 triangles at 0.04 and 9 254 at 0.02 leave it within 2·10⁻³ and 1.3·10⁻³
only.
The neutral coated cylinder of §119, meshed by its rings, keeps the conductivity and
the plane bulk modulus of its matrix within 2.9·10⁻⁶ and 1.5·10⁻⁶ at the size 0.1, five times
closer than its level sets (1.5·10⁻⁵ and 6·10⁻⁶); shells of fibres have their areas to
10⁻⁶, and coated spheres the coatings of their cuts. The fibres of the square array filling 0.4 of the plane have their area within
6·10⁻⁶ at the size 0.1, 7.9·10⁻⁷ at 0.05 and 5·10⁻⁸ at 0.025, the fourth power of the size
(8·10⁻³, 3·10⁻³ and 8·10⁻⁴ off with the straight edges between the nodes of the circles,
the chords: its square); the cuts of hardcore spheres theirs within 2·10⁻⁶ at the size 0.04;
the conductivity of the array against Perrins et al. within 1.4·10⁻⁵ (conducting) and
9·10⁻⁶ (insulating, the pores left out) at the size 0.05, 2·10⁻³ and 3·10⁻³ off with the
chords, and Keller's product within 6.7·10⁻⁵ and 9.3·10⁻⁶ at 0.1 and 0.05 — as the level sets
do at about half the size, whose remeshing refines the circles beyond the size of the
elements to keep its Hausdorff distance. A random bed of 21 fibres of radius 3.5 filling half
of a periodic square of edge 40, gaps of 0.3 at least, is meshed in 0.35 s by 12 140
triangles at the size 1, its smallest angle 17°, its pores in one part; its level sets need
a grid of 0.1 for that, and 3.6 s (§120). A circle that barely crosses a side of the box, or
passes by one of its corners, leaves a thin cap there, whose sharp tips the elements take:
over twenty realizations of the template `fibre_bed_plane` the smallest angles go from 1°
(a cap 0.002 thick) to 19°, 10° in the median, the elements valid all the same.

**Exact contours.** The sections of oblique and wavy fibres — the chains of spherocylinders
of `long_fibers` with `misalignment`, oblique segments with round caps, and spheres among
them — are not discs: their contours are traced (`mesh.contours`). A point of the plane lies
within a radius of an axis only if the axis comes within a radius of the plane: the axes,
clipped to the slab $|z' - z| \le r$, keep the section (`section_capsules`; their periodic
images along $z$ taken). The capsules whose axes come closer than the sum of their radii are
grouped into bodies (`section_bodies`: the pairs of a k-d tree, the distances of segments by
their closest points, Ericson 2005, §5.1.9), the images across a periodic box apart: the
sections of different bodies, those of disjoint sets, do not meet. Each body's contours are
traced on its own signed distance $d_b(x) = \min_k (\operatorname{dist}(x, a_k) - r_k)$ over
its axes $a_k$, exact outside it: by the marching squares on a grid of its own, of an eighth
of its least radius (`TRACE_CELLS`), the saddles resolved by the mean of their corners, each
vertex then moved along its edge of the grid onto the surface by Newton's method, kept within
the edge by bisection, to round-off: the contours keep the topology of the marching squares,
which do not cross, where steps along the gradient of $d_b$, the least of the distances to
several capsules, can jump from a surface to another. The level sets of the whole section (above) close the
gaps narrower than their background; these stay open, however narrow. `contour_mesh` meshes
them as the discs: the contours cut where they cross the lines of the sides (the crossings
moved onto the surface along the side by Newton's method; where it crosses the line at a
grazing angle, whose steps overshoot, bracketed by the first change of sign from the
chord's crossing outward, then refined within the bracket; near a corner of the box, the
crossings of the two lines in turn along their edge as their points on the surface, which
may come in the other order than along the chord), the pieces inside the box kept,
their nodes on the surfaces at sizes graded from the gaps — the distances $d_b$ of the other
bodies at the vertices of a contour, exact — and from their curvatures, $2\pi\rho/24$ for the
radius $\rho$ of the circle through three vertices; the sides match, `mmg2d` meshes the
regions within the contours, each triangle the phase of its centroid, and the six-node
elements have their middle nodes on the surfaces. The section of a straight fibre of radius
0.2 turned by 0, 30 and 50° is an ellipse of area $\pi r^2/\cos\theta$: across a side of
the periodic box, within 8.4·10⁻⁶, 6.5·10⁻⁶ and 2.1·10⁻⁶ at the size 0.05, 5.2·10⁻⁷,
3.8·10⁻⁷ and 2.3·10⁻⁷ at 0.025 (2.6·10⁻³ to 1.3·10⁻³ off with the chords).

Where the capsules of a body cross, its contours have corners. Where a contour passes from
the surface of a capsule to that of another, the point of both surfaces near its two
vertices, by Newton's method on their two distances, is inserted on the edge near them that
it lengthens the least: a node of the pieces on either side; the sizes are graded toward
the sharp ones (more than 10° between the normals, `CORNER_ANGLE`) as toward the corners of
the unions of discs, and the middle node of each edge of a piece is moved onto the capsule
on whose surface its two ends lie, where the least of the distances would take the other
surface near a corner. Where a contour passes from a capsule to another that it does not
cross, its chord outside the body, it bridges a gap between them narrower than a cell: the
body is traced again on grids four, sixteen and sixty-four times as fine
(`TRACE_REFINEMENTS`, their distances in a band about the surface, four million nodes at
most). The sizes take the gaps within a contour (to its vertices farther
along it than three times their distance: the two sides of a narrow wedge) and between the
contours of a body; where a gap $g$ is narrower than the bulge of chords of the least size,
they fall to $\sqrt{2\rho\,g}$, chords that bulge by a quarter of it; the contours within
three times the least size, holes and the tips of caps, are left out; and the edges are
checked before `mmg2d`: two that cross leave the section to the level sets. Two discs of
radius 0.2 whose centres are 0.3 apart are meshed by their contours as by the union of
discs, within 3.3·10⁻⁶, 3.7·10⁻⁷ and 2.5·10⁻⁸ of their area at the sizes 0.05, 0.025 and
0.0125, their corners to round-off; two discs of radius 0.1 that a third joins, their
circles 0.002 apart, the gap followed on the grid four times as fine, within 6.4·10⁻⁶ and
4.9·10⁻⁷ at 0.05 and 0.0125, as by the union of discs. The sections of Boolean networks of
spherocylinders turned at random (radius 0.03, length 0.4): filling a tenth of a periodic
cube, the twelve meshes of six realizations at the sizes 0.05 and 0.025 within 2.1·10⁻⁶ of
counts on grids of 4000² points; filling a fourth, the twelve within 4.7·10⁻⁶ at both sizes
alike (the errors of the counts), where the level sets are 3.9·10⁻³, 1.3·10⁻³ and
4.3·10⁻⁴ off at the sizes 0.05, 0.025 and 0.0125 for the first. The size field of the
contours is the least over all their points: those of a contour traced finely, on the finer
grids of a body's gaps, would hide among the nearest a smaller size a little farther — the
round tip of a capsule cut by a single chord, 3.4·10⁻⁵ of the box. `mmg2d` (5.7.0) does not
triangulate some inputs the same way from a run to another — the same file of contours,
run six times, gave two meshes, their interior nodes moved —, so that a mesh of the plane
is reproducible to the bit only where it does. Three
features of these sections are narrower than the cells of the grids. A wedge of matrix
between two capsules that cross at a small angle, narrower than a cell about a node of the
grid in it: the marching squares close a loop of their own about the node, inside the
contour that passes around the wedge to its corner; a loop within 16 cells that holds no
other, whose inside is already of the phase of the body there (its distance at the point
of the loop farthest from its edges) between the other loops of the body, is left out.
Three surfaces that meet nearly at a point: the contour passes from the first to the
second along the third for less than a cell (10⁻⁵ in a realization), the point of the
first two covered by the third, whose corners with each of them it then takes. And the
gaps between two capsules of a body narrower than a cell, which the grids four and sixteen
times as fine follow: a grid's distances are computed only in the cells of the last that
the surface may cross and in their neighbours — the distance changes by no more than the
distance between two points, so that a cell with a corner farther from the surface than
its diagonal is of one sign —, the marching squares on the edges between nodes known, and
their contours those of the whole grids, the nodes of a band about the surface: a tenth of
the time on the largest bodies, which span the box (0.86 × 0.57 at the sixteenth of a cell
of 3.75·10⁻³: 9 million nodes for the whole grid).

Every corner of a body, two of its capsules crossing where no other covers them, is also
found on its own: along a polygon of the section of each capsule (its boundary on 64 rays
from the point of its axis nearest to the plane, the section convex), where the distance
to another changes its sign, by Newton's method on the two distances. A corner that the
contours do not take is a feature smaller than a cell, which the finer grids follow; a
corner far from the contour, at the tip of a narrow wedge of matrix that the grid cut, is
inserted where the contour passes from one capsule to the other, sixteen cells away at
most; and a contour may pass from a capsule to another without a corner only where the two
share an end (a joint of a chain) or where its two vertices lie on both surfaces: elsewhere
it is a corner that the grid did not resolve, and the body is traced again.

A ply of fibres of radius 0.05 misaligned by 3° filling half of a periodic cube, 74
sections in its middle plane with gaps down to 4·10⁻⁴: the level sets close its gaps — 7
parts of fibres at the size 0.05 and 15 at 0.025, 2.7·10⁻² and 8·10⁻³ too much fibre —, its
contours keep the 74 apart, their area within 5·10⁻⁶ of a count on a grid of 4000² points,
by 50 006 triangles in 2.4 s (the level sets: 5 982, the narrow gaps not graded), and the
reciprocal theorem of Keller and Mendelson holds within 3.6·10⁻⁴ and 2.7·10⁻⁴ at the sizes
0.05 and 0.025. Its pores stay in one part, which the bridges of the
level sets split into 25: across the fibres, along $x$, its permeability (§120) is 2.0·10⁻⁶
on the contours and 2·10⁻⁹ on the level sets.

**The axial stiffness of misaligned plies.** The section of a ply is solved as that of
straight fibres along $z$: its transverse moduli are those of the ply where the fibres wave
little, its axial ones are not. Its stiffness $C$ turned so that its axis follows each
segment of the fibres, $C_{ijkl}(d) = R_{ip} R_{jq} R_{kr} R_{ls} C_{pqrs}$ for the least
rotation $R$ that takes $e_3$ to the direction $d$ of the segment (about $e_3 \times d$, the
transverse axes kept as near $x$ and $y$ as they can be: `turned_stiffness`), and averaged
with the volumes of the segments (`fibre_directions`), gives the Voigt and Reuss bounds of
the stiffness of the ply, the composite aligned with each segment about it
(`misaligned_stiffness`; Hill 1952): the average of the turned stiffnesses and the inverse
of the average of their compliances. Layers normal to $z$, each of one orientation, the
strains in their plane and the stresses on it continuous (Backus 1962), give the stiffness
of fibres that all wave together, between the two. One direction turned by $\theta$ gives
the modulus of the laminates, $1/E = \cos^4\theta/E_L + \sin^4\theta/E_T + (1/G_{LT} -
2\nu_{LT}/E_L)\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta$, to round-off. Plies of carbon fibres of radius
3.5 filling 0.45 of a box of 25 × 25 × 100 in epoxy, 1.2 apart at least, against the FFT
solution of their voxels of 0.35 (the gaps three voxels at least: the voxels of the
denser plies, 0.2 apart, bridge their gaps and double their transverse moduli): misaligned
by 3° (RMS), an axial modulus of 96.8 GPa between 94.0 (Reuss) and 100.7 (Voigt), where
the section gives 101.3; by 6°, 86.5 between 78.0 and 99.2 (101.8); aligned, 101.3 and
101.2. Fibres that all wave together, by 4°: 93.8, nearer to the layers and Reuss (89.9)
than to Voigt (100.3). The waviness of the ply of the tutorial, 3°, costs up to 5 % of its
axial modulus (122.6 to 128.5 GPa, its section 129.3). The runs record the three averages
of the stiffness of each section and condition beside it (`homogenization.misaligned`:
`stiffness_voigt.<bc>.<entry>`, `stiffness_reuss`, `stiffness_layers`); the segments of
coated fibres are those of the union the coating covers, those of hollow ones the fibres
about their lumens. So are the conductivities and the tensors of the other transport
phenomena, turned as $K(d) = R K R^T$ (`turned_conductivity`) and averaged the same way
(`misaligned_conductivity`; `conductivity_tensor_voigt.<bc>.<entry>`...): the layers, the
gradient in their plane and the flux across them continuous. Directions in the plane $xz$
give the axial conductivities $k_L \cos^2\theta + k_T \sin^2\theta$, whose mean is that of
Voigt and harmonic mean that of the layers, to round-off. The ply of the template
`misaligned_ply_plane` (3°): an axial conductivity of 5.632 W/m/K for its section, 5.619
(Voigt, the layers) and 5.560 (Reuss) for the ply.

**The thermal expansion of misaligned plies.** The expansion of the composite aligned with
each segment, turned as $a(d) = R a R^T$, and its stiffness $C(d)$ give that of the ply
under a uniform strain, $\langle C \rangle^{-1} \langle C a \rangle$ (the mean stress free),
under a uniform stress, $\langle a \rangle$ (each part free to expand), and that of layers
normal to $z$, each of one orientation (`misaligned_expansion`): the strains in their plane
$e = \langle M \rangle^{-1} \langle M a_t \rangle$, where $M = C_{tt} - C_{tn} C_{nn}^{-1}
C_{nt}$ is the stiffness of a layer in its plane under no normal stress ($t$ the strains 11,
22, 12, $n$ the stresses 33, 23, 31, in Voigt's engineering notation), and the strains
normal to them $\langle a_n + C_{nn}^{-1} C_{nt} (a_t - e) \rangle$. They are estimates, not
bounds. The FFT solution of a laminate of the composite cylinders along four directions, a
voxel each, has the stiffness and the expansion of the layers to round-off. The ply
misaligned by 5° above (carbon at −0.5·10⁻⁶ /K in epoxy at 60·10⁻⁶): along the fibres,
1.05·10⁻⁶ for its section and 1.354·10⁻⁶ by the FFT solution of its voxels of 0.4, within
1 % of the layers (1.366·10⁻⁶) and of a uniform stress (1.369·10⁻⁶), where a uniform strain
gives 0.79·10⁻⁶. Five degrees of waviness raise the axial expansion of the ply by 29 %,
which its section misses: the fibres that lean let the matrix expand along the ply; the
three degrees of the template `misaligned_ply_plane` raise it by 13 % (0.449·10⁻⁶ for its
section, 0.506·10⁻⁶ for the ply). The runs record the three with the stiffness
(`thermal_expansion_layers.<bc>.A33`...).

Coated and hollow fibres (the model `coating`) are meshed by the contours of their layers
(`section_layers`): the union and that grown by the thickness of the coating, or the union
shrunk by that of the shells and the union, the phases between them, the gaps across a
coating the distances of the bodies of the other layer. Coatings that meet, which the rings
leave, are bodies of their own. The core and the coating of an oblique fibre (radius 0.15,
coating 0.05, turned by 30°) are within 3.4·10⁻⁷ and 1.8·10⁻⁷ of their ellipses at the size
0.05; hollow fibres misaligned by 3° (shells 0.015 thick about bores of a third phase),
within 5·10⁻⁶ of counts on grids of 4000² points, where the level sets fail (`mmg2d` takes
their curves for non-manifold); two coated discs whose coatings cross, within 7·10⁻⁷ and
3.7·10⁻⁷. Coatings that percolate across the box, one body with its images: where two of
them barely meet, the grid of 0.016 cut the tips of the wedges of matrix between them
(2.5·10⁻⁵ of the box), which the corners found on their own restore: their cores and
coatings within 1.4·10⁻⁶ and 4.5·10⁻⁶ of counts on grids of 4000² points at the sizes 0.05,
0.025 and 0.0125 alike. Hollow fibres whose lumens are a union of their own (the union of
the fibres less that of their lumens: `hardcore_fibers` and `curved_fibers` with a
`lumen`) are meshed the same way, the lumens a layer within the fibres, of the phase of
the matrix: the walls of dense hardcore fibres (radius 0.04, a fourth of the box, lumens
of six tenths of the radii) within 6.1·10⁻⁶ of counts on grids of 8000² points, twelve
realizations of twelve at the size 0.05.

A combination of unions (`combination` with the operation `union`) is one union, its
capsules those of all: spheres and Boolean cylinders together within 9·10⁻⁷ of a count on
a grid of 4000² points, and, two of its cylinders 4·10⁻⁵ apart, traced on the grid
sixty-four times as fine, within 5.6·10⁻⁶. The difference of a union and of several (the operation
`difference`) is meshed as the union of those removed within the first, the phases 0, 1, 0
from the innermost: exactly where they lie within it, as lumens; where they cut its
contour, the contours of the two layers cross, and the section is left to the level sets.

The angle of a corner is that of the normals of the two contours in the plane, those of
the surfaces of the capsules projected onto it and normalized: unnormalized, the normals
that tilt out of the plane made it larger (a corner where two contours are tangent came
out at 53°). Two contours that meet within half a degree (`TANGENT`) are tangent, not a
corner: where a chain of capsules bends, the round end of a capsule and the side of the
next meet tangentially, at a point that Newton's method places poorly (the trace and the
pairs of capsules 4·10⁻⁸ apart, where they should agree to 4·10⁻⁹), and the check of the
corners of the contours against those of the pairs of capsules took it for a corner that
the trace missed, leaving the chain to the level sets.
Curved fibres, worm-like chains of short segments (radius 0.03, ten segments of 0.04 that
bend by some 16° at each joint, a tenth of the box), solid or hollow, apart or overlapping,
are meshed by their contours within 2.6·10⁻⁶ of counts on grids of 8000² points at the
sizes 0.05 and 0.025, the noise of the counts (the same mesh differs from counts on grids
of 4000², 8000² and 16000² points by 3·10⁻⁷, 2.5·10⁻⁶ and 1.4·10⁻⁶).

**Contours that graze a side.** A contour that crosses the line of a side at a grazing
angle dips across it by little: by less than the bulge of the chords of its trace (up to a
256th of its radius, the cells an eighth of it), its two crossings then between two
vertices on the same side of the line. Between two such vertices, nearer to the line than
their chord is long, the point of the surface farthest across the line (golden sections
over the chord, each point projected onto the capsule or the face of both ends) is taken
among the vertices where it lies across: the chords then cross the line twice, the piece of
the contour in the box ends on it, and the lens of its image across the side is meshed.
Each crossing is the root between the points of the line beside the ends of its edge, where
the distance has their signs: the root nearest to the crossing of a chord with one vertex
in the dip may be that of the other side of it. Along a side that it crosses, a contour
that runs within 15° of it (`GRAZING`) is graded by its gap to the side, as by the gaps to
the sides it does not cross: the wedges between the contour and the side and the lens of
its image are thin, and their triangles, spanning them flat, folded with their curved
edges, which were then straightened. An oblique fibre (10°, radius 0.2) whose ellipse dips
10⁻⁵ across a side — the nodes of its piece fell out of the box, and the section to the
level sets — is within 5.5·10⁻⁶ of its area at the size 0.05, relatively (8.3·10⁻⁶ away
from the sides); dense hardcore fibres (radius 0.04, a fourth of the box), twelve
realizations meshed by their contours where one fell to the level sets, within 3.2·10⁻⁶ of
counts on grids of 8000² points (1.4·10⁻⁵ before, one crossing at 10° whose lens was a
single flat triangle). Capsules that touch in space (the fibres of random walks, rolled
against each other) have sections apart unless the point of contact is in the plane: they
are bodies of their own, the narrow gap between their sections graded as any, and only
those whose point of contact is within a thousandth of their radius of the plane (or that
touch along a line, parallel) leave the section to the level sets — two oblique capsules
that touch 0.02 below the plane, within its slab, their sections 0.0029 apart, within
9·10⁻⁶ of the area of their two ellipses, relatively (1.4·10⁻⁵ for one alone, its contour
in 24 arcs a circle at both sizes 0.05 and 0.025); random walks of fibres in contact, solid
and hollow, within 3.2·10⁻⁶ of counts on grids of 8000² points, the bias of the counts (one
within 5.1·10⁻⁶, 2.9·10⁻⁶ and 1.4·10⁻⁶ of counts on grids of 4000², 8000² and 16000²
points). A vertex of a contour on the line of a side (a corner on the side, where the
distance along the line is not smooth) is the crossing itself, and a corner where a contour
crosses a side is that crossing, a node of the side: the lattices of struts, whose nodes
lie on the faces of their cells, are meshed by their contours, every cell of
`strut_lattice` solid and hollow, cut at two heights, its areas within 10⁻⁶ at the sizes
0.05 and 0.0125 (within 10⁻⁸ through the middle of the cells, their struts there mostly cut
along their axes) — the section of the octet cell through its middle, its diagonal strips,
$4\sqrt{2}\,r - 8 r^2$ to round-off. `mmg2d` inserts the nodes in their order and may fail
among many collinear ones, the straight sides of struts cut along their axes: it is run
once more with the nodes in another order. Features too small for the finest grid and
contours tangent to a side, two of their crossings within a hundredth of the least size,
are left to the level sets.

**Flat caps.** A cylinder whose flat cap reaches the slab of the plane keeps that end (the
ends clipped to the slab are round, which keeps the section): its distance is that of the
finite cylinder between the planes of its flat ends, exact — the radial excess $u = \rho -
r$ and the axial one $s$ beyond the nearer plane, $\max(u, s)$ inside and along a face,
$\sqrt{u^2 + s^2}$ beyond the rim —, and of the balls of its round ends, the least. Its
section is that of the lateral surface cut by the lines of its caps, with the corners of
its rims where the contour passes from a face to another: Newton's method on the lateral
distance and on that of the plane of the cap, the faces of the vertices of the trace those
of the pieces of the distance. The nodes of a piece of contour, and the middle nodes of the
six-node elements, go onto the face of both ends of their edge — the lateral surface (as
if the ends were round) or the plane of the cap, where they stay straight —, not onto the
cylinder, whose larger face would take the nodes of a thin wedge across to the cap. Where
the corner of two capsules lies on a cap, the rim between it and the vertex of the trace
on the lateral surface is taken too, the corners of one change inserted in turn on the
edge that their path lengthens the least; a contour that its corners knot is traced on a
finer grid. One oblique cylinder (40°, radius 0.15) whose flat end cuts the plane, its
section an ellipse cut by a line: within 5.6·10⁻⁶, 7.4·10⁻⁷ and 4.9·10⁻⁸ of the area of the
segment of the ellipse at the sizes 0.05, 0.025 and 0.0125, the corners of its rim nodes
of the mesh. Boolean networks of cylinders with flat caps (radius 0.03, length 0.4), which
all fell to the level sets: filling a tenth and a fourth, the twelve meshes of six
realizations at the sizes 0.05 and 0.025 of each by their contours, within 1.6·10⁻⁶ and 7·10⁻⁶ of counts
on grids of 8000² points (those of 4000² points are off by up to 6·10⁻⁶ along the straight
edges of the caps). The coating of flat caps is the union grown by its thickness $t$, the
points within $t$ of it: its distance that of the union less $t$, its caps moved out by
$t$ and its rims round, a surface without corners whose nodes and middle nodes go onto that
distance (not onto round caps of the radius grown, which bulge into the matrix); the cores
of shells are the union shrunk, the caps moved in and the rims sharp, their faces moved
with them. Boolean cylinders (radius 0.04, filling a tenth) coated and hollowed by 0.012:
the fractions inside each union within 4.6·10⁻⁶ of counts on grids of 4000² points, at the
sizes 0.05 and 0.025.

**Exact sections of tessellations.** The power distance of a point $(x, y, z)$ of the plane
$z$ to a germ $(x_k, y_k, z_k)$ of weight $w_k$ is $|(x, y) - (x_k, y_k)|^2 - (w_k - (z -
z_k)^2)$: the section of a Laguerre (or Voronoi) tessellation in space by the plane is the
power diagram of the plane of the germs projected on it with the weights
$w_k - (z - z_k)^2$ (`section_weights`), the nearest image of each germ along $z$ in a
periodic box — the farther ones, at the same point of the plane with smaller weights, have
empty cells, as have the germs whose cells the plane misses. `plane_mesh` meshes the sections
of the tessellations (and of the grains of seeds in space) by these exact polygons, those of
other structures by their level sets: the section at $z = 0.37$ of a Laguerre tessellation of
60 cells in a periodic unit cube has the areas of its 19 cells to round-off, which 200 000
points of the plane sampled in the cells find within their standard errors.

**Honeycombs.** The walls of prismatic cells (the model `honeycomb`: hexagonal, square and
Voronoi cells, their prisms along $z$) are the points of each cell nearer to its sides than
half its wall $t_i$; in a convex cell the distance to its boundary is the least of those to
the lines of its sides, so that its lumen is the intersection of its half planes moved in
by $t_i/2$, an exact convex polygon (`mesh.cells.cell_lumens`), and the walls the rest of
the box. `plane_mesh` meshes them by these polygons (`cells_mesh`): the edges of the lumens
graded across the thinnest wall (three elements) and from their gaps to the sides of the
box that they do not touch, the side nodes of a periodic box matching, `mmg2d` within them,
run once more in another order of the nodes where it fails. The prisms do not vary along
$z$: the mesh of their plane is the structure itself, and its stiffness and conductivity in
space are those of generalized plane strain. Square and hexagonal honeycombs (cells of 1,
walls of 0.1) in periodic boxes of whole cells have their walls $1 - (1 - t/d)^2 = 0.19$ to
round-off; Voronoi ones, in periodic boxes or with free sides, within 4.6·10⁻⁶ of counts of
their own distance on grids of 4000² points (10⁻⁵ on those of 2000²). A hexagonal honeycomb
of a solid, its lumens empty, has along its prisms the uniform strain for its field, its
axial modulus and conductivity those of the solid times the fraction of its walls, to
round-off (13.3 = 0.19·70 GPa); across them it is isotropic as its hexagonal symmetry has
it (its moduli $E_1$ and $E_2$ within 2·10⁻⁴), $E_1/E_s = 0.0129$ for walls of a sixth of
their length, 8 % above the beams of Gibson and Ashby in bending alone
($4/\sqrt{3}\,(t/l)^3 = 0.0120$), the stiff nodes of the walls. The radial files of wood
and prisms along another axis are left to the level sets.

**Maps of grains.** An orientation map (EBSD, the model `ebsd`: a lattice of one cell
through the thickness of the box, the label of a grain and its mean orientation per cell) is
meshed in its plane by its pixels (`lattice_mesh`): two triangles per pixel along the
diagonals that alternate with its parity, each the grain of its pixel, the grain boundaries
the edges of the pixels as the map measures them; the configurations of the model mesh it so
by default (`mesh.plane: auto`), the finite elements of the plane turning the crystals by the
orientations of their grains — where the tetrahedra of the lattice field, meshed by its
phases, had none. A window of 32 × 24 points of the demonstration map of nickel (20 grains,
1 536 six-node triangles) gives the bulk modulus of the crystals, 180.367 GPa, under every
condition (the mesher in space extrudes the same triangles through the box, each tetrahedron
the grain of its pixel), and the Young's modulus $E_1$ 206.6 GPa under kinematic conditions, 196.6 GPa under
static ones, about the 203.2 GPa of the FFT solver on its voxels.

**Elasticity of the plane.** The fields of a structure invariant along $z$ under a uniform
macroscopic loading do not vary along $z$: $u = E\,x + w(x, y)$, the strain
$\varepsilon = E + \operatorname{sym}\nabla w$ with $\partial_z = 0$, so that
$\varepsilon_{33} = E_{33}$ is uniform and the anti-plane component $w_3$ gives the shears
$2\varepsilon_{13} = 2E_{13} + w_{3,1}$ and $2\varepsilon_{23} = 2E_{23} + w_{3,2}$. In
*generalized plane strain* (`plane: generalized`, the default) the three components of $w$ are
unknowns, and the six components of $E$ give the 6 × 6 apparent stiffness of the structure in
space: the anti-plane shears couple to the plane through the crystals whose axes leave it. In
*plane strain* (`plane: strain`) $w_3 = 0$: the block 11, 22, 12 is the stiffness of plane
strain, stiffer (the shears 13 and 23 uniform). Conduction: $T = G\cdot x + w(x, y)$, the
3 × 3 tensor of the structure. Under periodic conditions $w$ takes the same values at the
facing nodes of opposite sides, the corners one node; under kinematic ones $w = 0$ on the
sides; under static ones the tractions $\Sigma n$ (the flux $Q\cdot n$) load the sides, the
displacement (temperature) is the unknown, its rigid motions removed — the three translations
