and the rotation about $z$ —, and the uniform components that no field of the plane gives are
unknowns of their own, dual to their stresses: $E_{33}$ (and $E_{13}$, $E_{23}$ in plane strain)
loaded by the area times $\Sigma_{33}$ ($\Sigma_{13}$, $\Sigma_{23}$), $G_3$ by $-A\,Q_3$. The
elements are integrated exactly on straight triangles (one point, or three of degree 2 for the
six-node elements), and the problems take the macroscopic loadings of the solvers in space —
mixed components condensed (§17), changes of temperature, named loadings — and give their
averages, energies, statistics of the phases and fields.

**The layer in space.** `TriMesh.extruded` cuts the prism over each triangle into three
tetrahedra along the diagonals of its sides from their least node — the cuts of neighbouring
prisms then match —, a layer periodic across its thickness. A function of the plane, linear
on a triangle, is linear on each tetrahedron of its prism and takes the values of the nodes
there: the four-node elements of the layer, its nodes tied across it, span the three-node
elements of the plane, and the periodic problems in space are those of the plane.

**Loading paths.** The nonlinear behaviours of the solvers in space (plasticity, crystal
plasticity, damage, finite strains...) follow the loading paths of a mesh of the plane on its
layer in space (`TriMesh.layer`): one layer of prisms of the thickness of its mean edge, cut
into tetrahedra (ten-node ones for six-node triangles), its faces $z$ tied as those of the
other axes — the fields do not vary across it, the thickness drops out of the averages, and the
periodic problems of the layer are those of the structure in generalized plane strain. Kinematic
conditions on the layer would clamp its faces $z$: its paths run under periodic conditions only
(the others skipped), and in generalized plane strain (not with `plane: strain`); their
tangents are factorized (`solver: auto`), the algebraic multigrid converging poorly on a layer
tied across its thickness — the tension of 658 six-node triangles of two phases in 22 s
instead of 207 s. A uniaxial
tension of a square of an elastoplastic matrix about a stiff disc gives the same response on
the mesh of the plane as on its layer itself, to round-off.

**Verification.** A homogeneous square gives its stiffness and conductivity under every
condition, for both orders and both hypotheses, to 10⁻¹². Three layers across $x$ of two
turned cubic crystals and an isotropic phase give the stiffness of the laminate — the
components 11, 12, 13 harmonic means across the layers, the others their corrected averages —
to 3·10⁻¹⁶, the strains being uniform in each layer. The checkerboard of two conductivities 1
and 10 tends to the geometric mean $\sqrt{10}$ of Dykhne from above, slowly, as the field is
singular at the corners of the squares: 13.9, 7.9 and 4.5 % above it on grids of 16, 32 and 64
squares of three-node elements, 5.4, 3.1 and 1.8 % of six-node elements; across the plane, the
arithmetic mean 5.5 exactly. The grains of seeds of the plane of cubic crystals
($c_{11} = 168$, $c_{12} = 121$, $c_{44} = 75$) give the same stiffness and conductivity in the
plane and on their extruded layer by the finite elements in space, to 10⁻¹⁵; their bulk
modulus is that of the crystals, 136.667, under every condition, and their stiffnesses are
ordered, kinematic above periodic above static ($C_{11}$ 196.3, 195.0 and 191.7).

**Files.** The meshes of the plane are written as plane elements of Abaqus and CalculiX (CPE3
and CPE6 in plane strain, CPS3 and CPS6 in plane stress; the sets of the phases, of the grains
and of the nodes of the sides; the crystals of each grain turned into the axes of the box,
`TYPE=ANISOTROPIC`, since a plane element takes no orientation out of its plane), as Gmsh
files (triangles of types 2 and 9, the edges of the sides as lines of types 1 and 8), VTK
files (cell types 5 and 22) and Medit files of dimension 2, and read back with their grains,
orientations, rectangle, periodicity, plane and thickness; the periodic equations of their
plane elements tie the two degrees of freedom of each node of the upper sides to those of its
image and of the reference nodes `REF_X` and `REF_Y`, the forces of a macroscopic stress
those of the areas of the sides times the thickness.

**In space and in the runs.** The mesher in space takes the columnar grains too
(`conforming_mesh`): their exact polygons extruded through the box in layers of about the
size of the elements, the faces of a periodic box matching, the faces $z$ among them — the
volume of each grain its area times the thickness to round-off —, for what only the
tetrahedra do (loading paths, Code_Aster, OpenFOAM). A configuration meshes the realizations
of seeds of the plane in their plane by default (`mesh.plane: auto`), the section of any
structure at `mesh.z` with `plane: true`, writes the triangles (`<stem>_tri.<format>`, the
plane elements of Abaqus with the crystals of the grains) and solves them by the finite
elements of the plane (`homogenization.plane`); its figures draw the triangles in the
colours of their phases and the fields of the solutions on them, deformed by their
displacement. `morphogen homogenize` meshes a geometry in its plane with `--plane` (by
default for the columnar grains), reads the meshes of the plane it wrote, and solves them.

Checked (`tests/test_plane_meshes.py`): the triangles counterclockwise, their sides, six-node
elements and layers of tetrahedra (three per triangle, the volume of the area times the
thickness); the columnar grains in space, the volumes of the grains, the faces matching; the power diagram of coplanar germs against the exact cells, periodic or not;
the grains of seeds of the plane meshed with the areas of the exact grains, angles above 3°,
matching sides; their small features removed (half the elements at most, angles above 5°,
the areas within 8 % and 1 % on average); the section of spheres against their level set on a fine grid; the files read
back; the uniform fields, the laminates, the checkerboard and the layer in space; `homogenize`
of a mesh of the plane (moduli, tensors, thermal expansion, named loadings, fields, porous
meshes), what it does not solve refused; the loading paths on the layer in space, under
periodic conditions only; an orientation map meshed by its pixels (two triangles each, their
grains and orientations, the bulk modulus of the crystals, a run); a run of seeds of the plane (its files of
triangles, the bulk modulus of the crystals), the keys of the configurations and what the
meshes of the plane do not take, the command line, the figures.

## 120. Creeping flow through the pores of the plane (`homogenization.plane_flow`)

**The problem.** A fluid of viscosity $\eta$ creeps through the pores of a rigid solid that
does not vary along $z$ — a bed of parallel fibres, the dry preform of a unidirectional
composite before the resin fills it, or the section of any structure — under a macroscopic
pressure gradient: the uniform force $f$ of the gradient drives the Stokes flow
$\eta \Delta v - \nabla p + f = 0$, $\nabla \cdot v = 0$ in the pores, $v = 0$ on their walls,
$v$ and $p$ periodic. The mean velocity over the whole cell, the solid included, obeys
Darcy's law, $\langle v \rangle = (k/\eta)\, f$, with a symmetric positive tensor $k$ that does
not depend on the fluid (§67). Since nothing varies along $z$, the component of the momentum
along $z$ is uncoupled: the flow across the fibres is a plane Stokes flow, the flow along
them the anti-plane flow $\eta \Delta w + f_3 = 0$, $w = 0$ on the walls — the problem of the
torsion of a bar, or of the conduction of §119 with the walls held at zero — and $k_{13} =
k_{23} = 0$.

**The elements.** The plane flow is solved by the elements of Taylor & Hood (1973): the
velocity quadratic on the six-node triangles of the pores, the pressure linear on their
corners and continuous, a stable pair (it satisfies the inf-sup condition of Brezzi), the
velocity of the third order in its values; the weak form
$\eta \int \nabla v : \nabla w - \int p\, \nabla \cdot w = \int f \cdot w$,
$\int q\, \nabla \cdot v = 0$ — the Laplacian form, the same flow as that of the symmetric
gradient for walls at rest and periodic sides. The elements are those of the plane (§119),
isoparametric, curved along the walls of the sections of the structures that give their
implicit functions; their integrals of the second degree at three points (exact on straight
elements). The anti-plane flow takes the same quadratic elements. The pores are the void
phases of the materials (or the phases `pores`), meshed with the solid (`mesh.phases: all`):
the walls are the edges between them and the other phases, or the free edges of a mesh of
the pores inside the box; the nodes of the walls, their corners and middle nodes, hold the
fluid at rest, and the nodes of the upper sides of the periodic box are those of their images.
The pressure, determined up to a constant in each connected part of the pores (connected
through the corners of their triangles and across the box), is fixed at one node of each:
the closed pores hold a fluid at rest — across the plane, for they are pipes along $z$. The
saddle point of the plane flow is factorized once (LU, a sparse factorization of SuperLU) for
the two forces $f = e_x$ and $f = e_y$, the anti-plane flow by another for $f_3 = 1$; the
mean velocities give the columns of $k$, symmetrized. With `fields`, the velocities of the
three flows at the nodes of the triangles of the pores come with them, and the runs write
them (`<stem>_hydraulic_permeability_periodic.vtu`: `velocity_x`, `velocity_y` and
`velocity_z`, under the unit forces along $x$, $y$ and $z$).

**The gaps.** The transverse permeability of a bed of fibres is that of its narrowest gaps,
whose flows are a few elements across: the mesh must keep them open. The discs of straight
fibres meshed by their circles (§119) have the elements graded from the gaps, three across
the narrowest. The sections meshed from the functions of their phases sampled on a grid
(`background`, §119) — oblique fibres, discs that meet, any other structure — need a grid
that resolves the gaps, a third of the smallest: a random packing of fibres of radius 3.5 at
0.5 of the area, gaps of 0.3 at least, meshed by its level sets with elements of 1 on the
grid of 0.5 (the default, half of the elements) lost 0.6 % of its pores in ten closed parts
and 5 % of its transverse permeability; on the grid of 0.1 it kept its pores to 10⁻⁶ in one
part, and its tensor within 2·10⁻⁴ of that on the grid of 0.05 — which its discs give at the
size 0.5 (0.044468, 0.12937 and 2.0606 for $k_{11}$, $k_{22}$ and $k_{33}$; 0.044493,
0.12941 and 2.0606 at 0.25).

**Checked** (`tests/test_plane_flow.py`): the channel of Poiseuille between plane walls along
the lines of the grid, its parabola in the quadratic elements to 10⁻¹³ at the nodes and its
permeability $H^3/12L$ along the channel and along $z$ to 10⁻¹², zero across; the square
arrays of cylinders across them against the drags $F/\mu U$ of Sangani & Acrivos (1982),
51.53 and 102.90 at the fractions 0.2 and 0.3, $k = \pi a^2/(cF) = 1/F$ for a unit cell:
within 1.1·10⁻⁴ and 3.9·10⁻⁵ on the curved triangles of their discs at the size 0.05 (the
digits of the drags; 1.8·10⁻⁵ and 1.1·10⁻⁴ on their level sets; 0.8 to 0.9 % off with the
chords), and along them against the series of Drummond & Tahir
(1984), $a^2(-\ln c - 1.476 + 2c - c^2/2)/(4c)$, which is 8·10⁻⁴ and 3·10⁻³ off; the
closed pores of the array of fibres taken as the pores, a fluid at rest across the plane
(10⁻⁷ of the flow along $z$) and the pipes of Hagen and Poiseuille along it,
$k_{33} = c\,a^2/8$, within 7.5·10⁻⁵, 6.1·10⁻⁶ and 3.7·10⁻⁷ at the sizes 0.1, 0.05 and
0.025 (1.7·10⁻⁵, 1.7·10⁻⁶ and 7.5·10⁻⁸ on the level sets); a random bed of twelve fibres of
radius 0.1 at 0.38 (gaps of 0.02), converged to 10⁻⁴ at the size 0.0125 ($k_{11}$
3.0598·10⁻⁴, $k_{22}$ 9.43·10⁻⁵, $k_{33}$ 3.4986·10⁻³ on its level sets, its discs within
7·10⁻⁴),
which the lattice Boltzmann method of §67 approaches on the voxels of its section, their
walls stairs in the gaps, from 7.4 % and 0.5 % below on 96² voxels and 3.1 % below on
192² across the fibres, 0.6 % along them; `homogenize` of a mesh of the plane (the
permeability under periodic conditions beside the stiffness under every condition, the pores
left out of the elastic problems), the pores left out of the mesh and the flow without
periodic conditions refused; the configurations (`method: fe` and `mesh.plane: true`, or
`auto`, which takes the finite elements of the plane) and a run.

## 121. Creeping flow through the pores of a conforming mesh (`homogenization.mesh_flow`)

**The elements.** The Stokes flow of §120 in space, on a conforming mesh whose pores are
meshed with the solid (`mesh.phases: all`, which the runs take for `hydraulic_permeability`):
the elements of Taylor and Hood on the ten-node tetrahedra of the pores — the velocity
quadratic, isoparametric, curved along the walls (§76), the pressure linear and continuous
on their corners —, the weak form of §120 integrated at the four points of the tetrahedra
(exact on straight ones), the walls the faces of the pores on the other phases or free
inside the box, the nodes of the faces of the box those of their images, the pressure fixed
in each connected part of the pores; the three forces $e_x$, $e_y$, $e_z$ give the columns of
$k$, and with `fields` the velocities of their flows at the nodes of the pores, which the runs
write as for the plane (§120). Where the lattice Boltzmann method of §67 draws the walls as
stairs, these follow them.

**The solver.** The saddle points of space fill fast when factorized: 27 516 unknowns (a
sphere in a periodic cube meshed at the size 0.2) take 140 s and 1.1·10⁸ entries of the
factors by SuperLU. Beyond 8 000 unknowns (`DIRECT_LIMIT`), MINRES solves them, preconditioned
by a block diagonal: a V-cycle of the smoothed aggregation of `homogenization.amg` on the
viscous block of each component, and the inverse of the lumped mass matrix of the pressures
over the viscosity, to which the Schur complement of the Stokes problem is spectrally
equivalent (Elman, Silvester & Wathen 2005): about a hundred iterations per force whatever
the mesh — 27 516, 62 411 and 131 829 unknowns in 9, 22 and 34 s, to the relative residual
10⁻⁸.

**Checked** (`tests/test_mesh_flow.py`): the channel of the plane on its layer of
tetrahedra (`TriMesh.layer`), the permeability of Poiseuille along it and along $z$ to
10⁻¹⁰ by the factorization and by MINRES, nothing across; a square duct of side 0.5, its
axial permeability on the layer as by the flow along $z$ of the plane within 7·10⁻⁶, and
within 4·10⁻⁴ of the series $0.0351443\,a^2$; the simple cubic arrays of spheres against
the drags of Zick & Homsy (1982), $k = 2a^2/(9cK)$ with $K$ = 4.292 at the fraction 0.125:
7.5·10⁻⁴, 2.2·10⁻⁴ and 5·10⁻⁵ below at the sizes 0.2, 0.12 and 0.08, the three axes alike,
and within 10⁻³ of $K$ = 7.442 at 0.216, the lattice Boltzmann method on 40³ voxels within
3 % of the elements; `homogenize` of a conforming mesh (periodic conditions; `acoustic` left to the
voxels) and a run with `method: fe` (`auto` keeps the voxels for the flows of space).
